Here's what I'd hope for: when I save a page, I want the app to keep its own copy of what the page said at that moment — almost like a snapshot. So even if the article later gets edited, paywalled, or taken down entirely, I've still got the version I cared about, and I can still open and read it.

And searching should lean on that saved copy. If I go looking months later for a phrase I remember, I'd want it to find my bookmark based on what the page said when I saved it — not come up empty just because the live page has changed and no longer has those words. The whole reason I'm saving things is so they don't slip away, so the collection should remember the page as it was to me, not only whatever it happens to be right now.

One related case: if the thing I saved is one of those PDF documents rather than a normal web page, I'd want the actual document itself kept, so I can still open the real file later. Can you show me how saving keeps that kind of copy?
